name: Beat Happening
label: K
lede: Three Evergreen students, no bass player, one borrowed drum kit and a label out of a kitchen: how the band people called childlike ended up helping throw a six-day festival SPIN called the true Woodstock of the '90s.

eras.title: A radio show, a kitchen label and a borrowed drum kit
eras.text: Calvin Johnson starts K Records to press tapes of his friends, then starts a band with two Evergreen classmates who don't own a full drum set. The plan is barely a plan: skip the bass, play all-ages rooms, fly to Japan with no shows booked.

years.src: Wikipedia: Calvin Johnson (musician) · Wikipedia: Heather Lewis (musician) · Wikipedia: K Records · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Calvin Johnson starts K Records at 19, selling tapes
years.p: K's first release, Survival of the Coolest, is a live eight-song set by the Supreme Cool Beings, taped off Johnson's KAOS radio show. Their drummer is [[Heather Lewis|6857ba96-db87-4daa-b048-527f79e48f53]].
years.xp:
Johnson had been a volunteer at Olympia's community station KAOS-FM since he was fifteen, in 1977. His first band, the Cool Rays, made its debut recordings with [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] in 1981, and by summer 1982 he was dubbing cassettes for local friends, according to Wikipedia.

Lewis, a New York transplant at Evergreen State College since 1980, took the Supreme Cool Beings drum stool over that summer break. Loud And Quiet adds that Johnson started the label after seeing the punk scene in Maryland and meeting [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]].

years.cap: Beat Happening in their early Olympia days
years.src: Wikipedia: Beat Happening · Wikipedia: Heather Lewis (musician) · Loud And Quiet · Exclaim! · Encyclopedia.com
years.h: Beat Happening: three Evergreen students, no bass, no drum kit
years.p: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]], Heather Lewis and [[Bret Lunsford|20db5f03-f625-4cfd-bab3-8a531b28c925]] start playing together. Lewis borrows drums from touring bands, or hits garbage cans and cardboard boxes.
years.xp:
The band took its name from Beatnik Happening, a student film. Wikipedia and Loud And Quiet disagree on whose girlfriend made it: Lunsford's, or Johnson's, [[Lois Maffeo|ab9605b4-3ef8-4dde-99c4-87abe0f769a2]]. The earliest recordings used maracas, a thrift-store Sears Silvertone guitar and an Echoplex, which Wikipedia says was there to bury the sound of Lunsford's guitar.

Wikipedia dates the band to 1982. Exclaim! puts the first gathering at August 26, 1983 in Anacortes, and the first four songs on tape December 11, 1983, at the Evergreen firehouse with [[Greg Sage|275a4de2-cdc4-445b-b17a-501b0f75e460]] of the [[Wipers|65aac2dc-216c-4b1a-8501-45567c901c0e]]. Johnson later told Encyclopedia.com: "We don't have a bass player. A lot of people were offended by that."

years.src: Exclaim! · Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Three Olympians fly to Tokyo with no shows booked
years.p: The trip lands them a first Japanese gig at a high school, through a former exchange student who knew Johnson. He also comes home with a tape by [[Shonen Knife|5089b746-7612-4a13-9153-33ff2560e161]].
years.xp: Exclaim! says they went without a single show lined up. Encyclopedia.com says Johnson found the Shonen Knife tape on that 1984 visit and put it out on K in 1985,

years.src: Exclaim! · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Henry Rollins heckles Johnson at a Black Flag show
years.p: Beat Happening plays the Tropicana, Olympia's all-ages punk club, on a [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] bill, and [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] heckles Johnson, per Exclaim!.
years.xp: The Tropicana had opened that March and became the scene's headquarters, according to Loud And Quiet. Johnson told the magazine that early performances "were clearly confrontational" and drew real animosity.

years.src: Exclaim! · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Our Secret / What's Important: K's first vinyl single
years.p: Johnson's label had only sold cassettes. Beat Happening's 7-inch is K's first record you can play on a turntable.
years.xp: A five-song cassette EP, Three Tea Breakfast, came out the same year on K, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Yellow cover, London calling
eras.text: A debut LP the color of a school bus reaches England by way of a music journalist. K gets its first hire. Screaming Trees show up with the back room of a video store.

years.src: Wikipedia: Beat Happening (album) · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Beat Happening: a crayon cat in a rocket ship
years.p: Ten songs, 19 minutes, recorded over sessions from November 1983 to February 1985 in Olympia and Portland. Melody Maker ranked it No. 27 among 1985's best albums.
years.xp:
Sessions ran through the Evergreen firehouse with Greg Sage, [[Pat Maley|abea0212-1041-4e34-a274-eea09f4da1e5]]'s Yoyo Studio (a converted chicken coop), two apartments and a live capture at the 13th Precinct in Portland. The cover is bright yellow with a crayon drawing of a cat in a rocket ship, per Loud And Quiet.

Wikipedia says [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Phil Elverum|9026f1f6-5cc1-4bcb-83c9-befb54ae7b82]] later praised how rudimentary it is.

years.src: Wikipedia: Beat Happening (album)
years.h: Johnson sells the LP to record stores himself; a critic sends it to London
years.p: Johnson peddles copies on a cross-country trip. Journalist Jerry Thackray, later known as [[Everett True|001897b1-fbb7-4dbe-b1df-ac638bf60afc]], hands it to Rough Trade, which releases it in Europe that year.
years.xp: The Rough Trade deal is how Beat Happening got in front of British indie fans years before most of America noticed. Wikipedia credits Thackray with pushing the record to the label.

years.src: Wikipedia: K Records · Wikipedia: International Pop Underground Convention
years.h: Candice Pedersen joins K for $20 a week and college credit
years.p: Pedersen becomes co-manager in 1986. By 1989 she is a full partner in the label.
years.xp: Wikipedia says K began in Johnson's kitchen. Pedersen's arrival is the point where it stops being one person with a tape deck. She and Johnson later co-organize the 1991 International Pop Underground Convention.

years.src: Wikipedia: Beat Happening/Screaming Trees · Life of the Record
years.h: One night, one cassette four-track, Screaming Trees
years.p: Beat Happening and [[Screaming Trees|bc5e6e42-73ba-44fa-a41e-3379402f0429]] record a four-song EP in the back room of the Conner family's video store in Ellensburg. Homestead Records puts it out in April 1988.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the store was New World Video. Life of the Record's oral history has Gary Lee Conner engineering it on a cassette four-track in a single night, with [[Mark Lanegan|a9126556-f555-4920-9617-6e013f8228a7]] singing alongside Johnson. The other three songs are "Tales of Brave Aphrodite," "Polly Pereguinn" and "I Dig You."

Wikipedia adds that a draft letter in [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s journal calls one of the tracks his favorite pop song of the 1980s.

years.src: Life of the Record
years.h: A borrowed distortion pedal and a fire escape: recording Jamboree
years.p: At Albright Productions in Ellensburg, Steve Fisk, Gary Lee Conner and Mark Lanegan work with a band that had rushed every earlier session. "Indian Summer" is written days before tape rolls.
years.xp:
Life of the Record's oral history has the band playing "Indian Summer" at just one show before recording it. The title track went down on the studio's fire escape for the ambient noise, "Hangman" worked on a single take and was never reliably repeated, and the album's one distortion pedal was an MXR borrowed from Johnson's brother Streator.

Johnson: "We had all of this time...we weren't in a hurry to get onto something else." Lewis called it "magical" and comfortable.

eras.title: The dark one, the rough one, the ashtray
eras.text: Jamboree gets real production, Black Candy gets rougher, and hardcore crowds on Fugazi bills don't enjoy either.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jamboree · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Jamboree: darker, louder, Lewis on two songs
years.p: K and Rough Trade release 11 songs in 23:58, with a guitar solo on "Midnight a Go-Go" from Screaming Trees' Gary Lee Conner. Heather Lewis sings only "In Between" and "Ask Me."
years.xp: NME gave it 9/10 and Pitchfork later scored it 8.6; The Village Voice gave it a B-minus, per Wikipedia. "Indian Summer" became the band's signature, covered by [[Luna|dda04604-b50a-4bd1-8780-77564c659dc0]] and [[Ben Gibbard|02031e5c-f9ab-4b4e-bc08-a61ea11a455d]]. Loud And Quiet says Kurt Cobain put the album on his list of 50 favorites.

years.src: Life of the Record: Notes
years.h: Europe, four months after Jamboree: The Pastels, The Vaselines, The Bats
years.p: A European run puts them on stages with Scottish and New Zealand indie bands. Lewis says crowds there "came and liked us."
years.xp: Life of the Record's account says the European tour began about four months after the American release of Jamboree and included dates with the Pastels, the Vaselines, the McTells and the Bats (in Germany). Lewis: "Touring in Europe was completely different."

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Candy
years.h: Black Candy: rougher, and Sonic Youth covers the title track
years.p: Recorded in 1988 with Steve Fisk, its title song is later covered by Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore of [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] with Epic Soundtracks.
years.xp: Reviews split. Author Dave Thompson wrote that the title track "kick[s] critical ass" while the rest sounds like the band didn't know it was recording. "T.V. Girl" gave the indie-pop act TV Girl its name, and Cub and [[Yo La Tengo|3f542031-b054-454d-b57b-812fa2a81b11]] each recorded "Cast a Shadow."

years.big: People were totally freaked out and pissed off that we were up on stage
years.src: Exclaim! · Wikipedia: Black Candy · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: A Fugazi fan throws an ashtray at Calvin Johnson in Los Angeles
years.p: Heather Lewis, quoted in Exclaim!, on the crowds when Beat Happening toured with [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]]. The ashtray came at the Country Club show.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Black Candy page says the band toured with Fugazi in 1990 and 1991. Exclaim! does not date the ashtray incident. Wikipedia also says Johnson's stage moves, a pogo, a hula and a shimmy taken from British punk news footage, were part of why hardcore crowds took it badly.

years.src: Wikipedia: Calvin Johnson (musician) · Wikipedia: Beat Happening · Wikipedia: International Pop Underground Convention
years.h: Kurt Cobain plays Johnson's KAOS show, K logo on his arm
years.p: Cobain sits in on Johnson's radio show, playing acoustic and singing a [[Wipers|65aac2dc-216c-4b1a-8501-45567c901c0e]] song as a duet.
years.xp: Cobain had the K Records logo tattooed on his forearm, saying it was to "try and remind me to stay a child." Wikipedia notes Nirvana's "Lounge Act" refers to the tattoo, and that Cobain played guitar on "Bikini Twilight," released by Johnson's side band The Go Team with [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]]. Nirvana was away on tour for the August 1991 International Pop Underground Convention, and Cobain said he was disappointed to miss it.

eras.title: Woodstock in Olympia
eras.text: Beat Happening moves onto Sub Pop's distribution, Johnson and Pedersen throw a six-day festival, and the trio makes its longest, strangest record before going quiet.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dreamy · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Dreamy: living room and studio, Sub Pop on the back
years.p: Steve Fisk produces the 30-minute record, recorded in 1990 in a living room and a professional studio. "Red Head Walking" and "Nancy Sin" ship as singles.
years.xp: Entertainment Weekly gave it an A and Pitchfork later scored it 8.6. Loud And Quiet quotes Johnson: "It was only when Sub-Pop released 'Dreamy' in 1991 that people started be like, 'Oh wait.'"

years.src: Wikipedia: International Pop Underground Convention · Wikipedia: K Records · Loud And Quiet
years.h: The International Pop Underground Convention takes over Olympia
years.p: Johnson and Candice Pedersen sell $35 passes for about fifty bands over six days, mostly at the Capitol Theater. Beat Happening plays too.
years.xp:
Fugazi, Bikini Kill, the Fastbacks, Built to Spill, the Melvins, Unwound and L7 were on it, along with [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] and Nation of Ulysses. Wikipedia says the pass was priced low so bands and venues got paid, and that people who came and didn't pay were welcome. Wikipedia's K Records article notes there was no hired security.

SPIN later called it "the true Woodstock of the '90s."

years.src: Wikipedia: International Pop Underground Convention · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Girl Night: Bratmobile, Heavens to Betsy, 7 Year Bitch, the Spinanes
years.p: The convention opens with a bill of women and queercore bands, built by Lois Maffeo, KAOS DJ Michelle Noel and shop owner Margaret Doherty.
years.xp: It became known simply as Girl Night and, per Wikipedia, took on near-legendary status among riot grrrls. Wikipedia's Beat Happening page says Heather Lewis, a woman drummer, inspired Kathleen Hanna, Kathi Wilcox and Molly Neuman.

q: I don't mind when we get called childlike, but I don't understand it.
years.src: Wikipedia: You Turn Me On · SPIN · Loud And Quiet
years.h: You Turn Me On: multitrack, and a nine-minute closer
years.p: Stuart Moxham of Young Marble Giants and Fisk produce the record, and the band uses multitrack for the first time. "Godsend" runs 9:28.
years.xp:
AllMusic called it "a masterpiece," Rolling Stone said it was vision, not chops, driving the band, and the Washington Post heard bubblegum hummability with punk dirges. Nine songs, 45 minutes: the longest album of their five.

Johnson told SPIN in 1993: "I don't mind when we get called childlike, but I don't understand it."

q: I didn't think I could do it anymore. I really didn't like being onstage.
years.src: Exclaim! · Loud And Quiet · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: The last tour ends in Lawrence, Kansas, and the band goes quiet
years.p: There is no announcement. Johnson says "Bret needed to take a break from things," and the trio never formally breaks up.
years.xp: Exclaim! quotes Lewis: "I didn't think I could do it anymore. I really didn't like being onstage." Lunsford tells the magazine the band "never became more important than our friendship." Band members have said they still practiced monthly, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Not broken up, just busy
eras.text: The trio never announces an ending. Johnson builds a studio and two more bands, Lunsford keeps a record store, and in 2000 they reconvene for one single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Calvin Johnson (musician) · Wikipedia: K Records
years.h: Johnson opens Dub Narcotic Studio; Beck and Modest Mouse record there
years.p: The studio doubles as [[Dub Narcotic Sound System|35968888-6cfb-4590-8f70-60886d0be91a]], Johnson's funkier band. [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]]'s One Foot in the Grave and early [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]] records come out of it.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the studio was set up around 1993 as both a recording space and a band. By 2016, it notes, K had money trouble and artists reporting unpaid royalties, and Johnson acknowledged the studio hadn't made the money he expected.

years.src: Wikipedia: Calvin Johnson (musician) · Loud And Quiet
years.h: Johnson and Doug Martsch of Built to Spill start the Halo Benders
years.p: [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]] and Johnson put out three albums together through 1998.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the group reunited for one show in Boise in 2008. Loud And Quiet has Johnson describing Beat Happening as on semi-permanent hiatus while he ran these projects.

years.src: Exclaim! · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Angel Gone: eight years later, one 7-inch
years.p: The trio reunites to record "Angel Gone" with [[Phil Elverum|9026f1f6-5cc1-4bcb-83c9-befb54ae7b82]], backed by "Zombie Limbo Time." It is their first new release since 1992.
years.xp: A second single, "Crashing Through" / "The This Many Boyfriends Club," followed in 2001, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Our Band Could Be Your Life · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Our Band Could Be Your Life gives them a chapter
years.p: [[Michael Azerrad|532857f4-2f6c-4e89-a280-1cdb68c3e6ec]]'s book on the 1980s American underground puts Beat Happening among its thirteen bands.
years.xp: Azerrad notes they widened the picture of a punk rocker beyond the mohawk-and-motorcycle-jacket type, per Wikipedia. Stephin Merritt of the Magnetic Fields reads the Beat Happening chapter on the audiobook.

eras.title: Boxed and sequenced
eras.text: K collects everything, Domino asks the band to pick their own best, and a discography that was once traded on cassette becomes a vinyl box.

years.src: Exclaim! · Wikipedia: Beat Happening
years.h: Crashing Through: every album and B-side in one box
years.p: Seven discs collect all officially released Beat Happening music, plus a Lois Maffeo essay and archival photos.
years.xp: Exclaim! says K printed 5,000 copies and sold out within months. Wikipedia says it leaves out only two tracks from a live cassette split with the Vaselines, and adds the rarities collection Music to Climb the Apple Tree By (2003).

years.src: Wikipedia: Bret Lunsford
years.h: Bret Lunsford writes the book on Anacortes
years.p: Lunsford, who ran the record store The Business from 1990 to 2005, publishes Images of America: Anacortes.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists him as owner of Knw-Yr-Own Records, a member of D+, and organizer of the What the Heck Fest in his hometown.

years.src: Wikipedia: Look Around · Exclaim!
years.h: Look Around: the band sequences its own 23-track best
years.p: Domino puts out a double LP the band chose and ordered chronologically, from "Our Secret" through "Angel Gone." Pitchfork scores it 8.2.
years.xp:
Exclaim! reported at the time that Beat Happening "have still not broken up" and had no plans to reunite. Lunsford lives in Anacortes and plays in D+, Lewis lives on an island in Puget Sound, and Johnson was touring solo.

AllMusic's Tim Sendra called the band "the kind of complementary bond most bands would kill to have."

years.h: We Are Beat Happening: the whole discography on vinyl
years.p: Domino issues a box set of the full catalog, with the band's and K's cooperation.
